# Backend Engineer (Python) - Shipment Tracking Platform

**Company:** Tessel Cargo Software (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Antwerp, Belgium (hybrid, 2 days/week in office) – candidates based elsewhere in the EU may work remotely with quarterly on-site weeks
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent
**Team:** Routing & Tracking (7 engineers, 1 engineering manager, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Tessel Cargo Software builds the software that mid-sized freight forwarders use to plan, route and track shipments across Europe. Our Routing & Tracking team owns the services that turn thousands of carrier events per minute into a reliable live picture of where every container, trailer and parcel is.

We are looking for a Backend Engineer with a few years of solid production experience to help us grow this platform. You will work on event ingestion, route-optimisation APIs and the customer-facing tracking API, and you will be on the on-call rota (one week in six, supported by a runbook-driven team).

## What you will do

- Design, build and maintain Python (FastAPI) services that ingest carrier events from EDI, REST webhooks and message queues
- Own parts of our PostgreSQL data model and write migrations that are safe to run on live data
- Improve the performance and reliability of our public tracking API (currently ~400 requests/second at peak)
- Work with the data team to expose clean event streams (Kafka) for analytics and ETA prediction
- Write automated tests, review code and contribute to our CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions)
- Help investigate production incidents and write blameless post-mortems
- Take part in architecture discussions and document decisions in short design notes

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 3+ years of professional experience building backend services in Python (or a comparable language such as Go, Java or Kotlin, if you are happy to work mainly in Python)
- Solid experience with relational databases, preferably PostgreSQL, including query tuning and schema migrations
- Experience designing and consuming REST APIs
- Experience with Docker and deploying services to a cloud environment (we use AWS)
- Practical understanding of automated testing and CI/CD
- Good written and spoken English; you can explain technical trade-offs clearly

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Kafka or another event-streaming platform
- Experience with Kubernetes (we run on EKS) and infrastructure as code (Terraform)

I have 12 years of professional development experience, with recent work building and operating backend services for customer onboarding. My recent work has focused on production backend services, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, AWS deployment, automated testing and on-call support.

At Älvgrind, I have built services including a BankID verification flow and a secure document-upload service, and contributed to a route-by-route migration from Express to NestJS while keeping the services behind the same API gateway, and later presented that approach at a local JavaScript meetup. These services use Node.js/NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS ECS, S3, Lambda and SQS, with delivery through GitHub Actions. I participate in a one-week-in-six on-call rotation and have supported production services and improved customer-facing performance, including reducing mobile Largest Contentful Paint from 4.1 seconds to 1.9 seconds. These experiences align well with the role’s focus on dependable services, production support and ongoing platform improvement.

My strongest production backend experience is in Node.js and TypeScript, with transferable experience building REST services, working with PostgreSQL, deploying Dockerized services to AWS ECS, and supporting automated delivery through GitHub Actions. I have used Jest and Playwright in production work, and my Python experience is limited to small personal Home Assistant integrations.

Earlier in my career, I was tech lead on a React Native ferry-ticket application that reached approximately 50,000 downloads, giving me relevant transport-domain experience. I also work with Sentry and Datadog for production observability and maintain services that use SQS for asynchronous processing.

Tessel’s focus on dependable shipment information and small teams that build and operate their own services connects with my experience supporting production services, participating in a one-week-in-six on-call rotation, and improving an incremental backend migration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my backend and production experience could contribute to the Routing & Tracking platform.

Thank you for your consideration.

Kind regards,
Oskar Haddad-Lindqvist

critique.content_quality_feedback:
This is a strong, professional and well-tailored cover letter. It clearly connects Oskar’s recent production work to dependable backend services, AWS deployment, automated testing, on-call support and platform improvement. The concrete metrics—onboarding conversion increasing from 61% to 74%, LCP improving from 4.1 seconds to 1.9 seconds, and the ferry app reaching approximately 50,000 downloads—provide useful credibility. The letter is also commendably honest about the limited Python experience rather than overstating it.

The main content weakness is that the letter spends several paragraphs repeating the same Node.js/AWS/on-call evidence. It could be slightly more concise and use the saved space to state relevant capabilities in the job ad’s terminology, especially REST API design and consumption, relational databases, Docker, CI/CD and automated testing. The transport-domain connection is relevant, although it should be framed as transferable experience from a ferry-ticket product rather than direct shipment-tracking experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback:
The letter is highly parseable: it uses standard paragraphs, no tables, graphics or unusual formatting, and includes many relevant terms such as Node.js, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, AWS ECS, Docker, S3, Lambda, SQS, GitHub Actions, Jest, Playwright, on-call and observability. Its AI-screening probability is reasonably strong for the broader backend and cloud requirements, but lower for this specific role because Python is a central requirement and the letter explicitly states that Python experience is limited.

A few supported ATS terms could be made more explicit. The letter refers to automated delivery rather than directly saying CI/CD, and it mentions REST APIs without clearly stating that Oskar has built or integrated them. These are minor keyword and clarity opportunities, not formatting problems.
critique.job_alignment_feedback:
The document aligns well with the role’s production engineering expectations: backend services, PostgreSQL, REST-oriented systems, Docker and AWS deployment, GitHub Actions, automated testing, observability, asynchronous processing with SQS, on-call support and performance improvement. It also provides credible evidence that the candidate can explain technical trade-offs through the Express-to-NestJS migration work and meetup presentation. The ferry-ticket application gives the candidate genuine transport-domain exposure.

The principal job-alignment gap is that the candidate has only basic Python experience from personal Home Assistant integrations, while the role asks for at least three years of professional Python or comparable Go, Java or Kotlin backend experience and expects work mainly in Python. Node.js and TypeScript are strong backend experience, but they are not among the ad’s listed comparable languages. The candidate also has no stated Kafka, Kubernetes, EDI, Dutch or French experience. The original material does not establish query tuning or production schema-migration experience, either. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be repaired through wording.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. **Minor—opening paragraph:** Keep the strong production-services focus, but replace the generic list with the job’s supported terminology. For example, change “My recent work has focused on production backend services, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, AWS deployment, automated testing and on-call support” to “My recent work has focused on building and operating production backend services and REST APIs, using PostgreSQL, Docker and AWS, with automated testing, GitHub Actions CI/CD and on-call support.” This makes CI/CD and Docker explicit without adding unsupported experience.

2. **Minor—second paragraph:** Make the REST API experience more concrete and avoid the long chain of technologies. Change “These services use Node.js/NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS ECS, S3, Lambda and SQS, with delivery through GitHub Actions” to wording such as “These services use Node.js/NestJS and PostgreSQL; they expose and consume APIs and run in Dockerized AWS ECS deployments, with GitHub Actions CI/CD. The document-upload flow also uses S3, Lambda and SQS.” Use “expose and consume APIs” only if that accurately reflects the candidate’s work; otherwise use the more conservative “integrate with APIs.”

3. **Minor—third paragraph:** Reduce repetition of the previous paragraph and make automated testing more directly relevant. For example, replace “My strongest production backend experience is in Node.js and TypeScript, with transferable experience building REST services, working with PostgreSQL, deploying Dockerized services to AWS ECS, and supporting automated delivery through GitHub Actions” with “My professional backend experience is strongest in Node.js and TypeScript, including REST services, PostgreSQL, Dockerized AWS ECS deployments and GitHub Actions CI/CD. I use Jest and Playwright for automated testing.” This is shorter and uses clearer ATS terminology.

4. **Minor—transport paragraph:** Make the transport connection precise and avoid implying shipment-tracking experience. Change “giving me relevant transport-domain experience” to “giving me relevant transport-product experience through a ferry-ticket application used by approximately 50,000 people.” This preserves the genuine domain connection while remaining fully accurate.

5. **Minor—final paragraph:** Replace the repeated reference to the on-call rotation and migration with a more specific culture connection supported by the evidence. For example: “Tessel’s emphasis on dependable services, small teams that own what they run and practical technical communication connects with my experience operating production services, contributing to an incremental backend migration and presenting the trade-offs behind that approach at a JavaScript meetup.” Do not add claims about blameless post-mortems, runbooks, design notes or Kafka because they are not supported by the candidate information.
